name: google_shopping_chromium
description: MEASURED 2026-09-02 -> 2026-09-05: this is the working Shopping twin -- 55 rows on `us` -- while google_shopping_camoufox ended on google.com/sorry on 9 of 9 runs (see its description); the `de`/`uk` exits drew 429 walls the same days. UPDATE 2026-09-05: timeout_ms 45000 -> 34000 (per-phase; see test_builtin_timeout_fits_the_first_attempt). The 45000 figures below are the 2026-08-28 state. Google Shopping tab (udm=28). Google's obfuscated class names change frequently (self_heal regenerates on drift). titles/prices are read per-card (div.PhALMc container) so they stay index-aligned; merchants is best-effort and may desync if a card omits the store; organic cards expose no per-card product URL (JS side-panel) so no url column is offered. Materializer lowercases country for gl= and derives lang for hl=. Product urls are NOT extractable: Google Shopping renders the cards with no <a href> at all (0 anchors across 55 live cards, 2026-07-26 — measured on Chromium, this preset's only engine before the 2026-08-27 split) and navigates via JS, so the field was removed rather than shipped permanently empty — an empty all=true field is not harmless, it trips row_alignment_mismatch on every successful run. ENGINE: Chromium (Playwright), stealth off. chromium_webgl_identity()'s host-aligned WebGL claim (an AMD Radeon 780M string under a Windows UA) does NOT apply here: it runs only inside stealth_config(), which src/browser/runner.py:194 reaches only when stealth is on, so this preset ships the browser's raw headless WebGL identity instead. No fingerprint_profile, which the Chromium runner would accept and ignore. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): THIS PRESET RETURNED NO DATA ON EITHER VARIANT — 0/6 runs each. This variant never reached a results page: 6/6 runs ended on google.com/sorry/index with all three retries spent — an ACCESS problem, unrelated to the wait strategy below, that this task does not fix. google_shopping_camoufox reached the requested …udm=28… URL on 4 of 6 runs (HTTP 200, block heuristic silent) and matched nothing there, and was sent to /sorry on the other 2. ROOT CAUSE SETTLED 2026-08-28 (task 5, by capture, on the Camoufox twin — this variant cannot reach the page to confirm the same shell, but shares this preset's parsing recipe and wait strategy so the fix ships on both): the reached-but-empty runs are Google's JS bounce shell, confirmed live 2026-08-28 on this exact udm=28 URL (90,802 bytes, DE, the same `table,div,span,p{display:none}` marker as google_search's capture, 0 #rso / div.PhALMc matches) — `wait_until: domcontentloaded` returns before Google's client-side check redirects away from it. Measured live (Camoufox): `wait_until: load` plus `wait_for_selector: div.PhALMc.bVO81.lLi9V` (the same node `titles` already reads) leaves the shell and resolves the redirect for real — landing on either the populated tab or google.com/sorry depending on whether the exit passes Google's JS check. This splits into two distinct, correctly-classified outcomes instead of one silent success: if the redirect leaves the page stuck on this shell (URL unchanged, not a recognised block endpoint), `wait_for_selector` genuinely times out and raises `selector_not_found: div.PhALMc.bVO81.lLi9V`, which `is_selector_miss()` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:132) treats as retry-worthy; if instead it lands on `google.com/sorry`, `redirected_to_block()` (src/browser/runner.py:1095, mirrored at src/browser/camoufox_runner.py:441) recognises the URL BEFORE `wait_for_selector` is ever called, skips the wait entirely (no extra latency over the old config), and the block classifier sets `blocked=True` with `"Captcha/block detected by heuristic"` — rotation then happens on `fetch_result.blocked` (src/queue/scrape_runner.py:646), not on a selector miss. Either way the old domcontentloaded-only config's single silent "0 rows, no error" stop is gone. Same shape and same fix as google_search (see that preset; also mirrors `yandex_search`'s wait_until=load + wait_for_selector). timeout_ms was already 45000 here, which already fits the 3-phase (warmup+goto+selector) budget at PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s on the fast-fail path (attempt 1 affordable ≈37.5s, shortened-and-logged, same arithmetic yandex_search runs on) but costs a real attempt in the pathological worst case: 3 phases each burning their full timeout afford only ONE full attempt before the 120s ceiling is spent (attempt 2 "not started"), where the old 2-phase config afforded two — a genuinely blocked run is not slower (see redirected_to_block above); only an ambiguously-stuck one pays the extra phase's time. This variant's own access block is UNCHANGED and NOT fixed by this task (still 6/6 at /sorry as of the audit, for this preset alone; not re-tested live here because it cannot reach the page at all). MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): 4/6 runs returned a REAL shopping SERP -- de 45 rows twice, uk 55, us 55, titles reading as real product listings (ASUS Vivobook, Lenovo V15 G4 AMN, HP 15-fd0211ng, Apple MacBook) -- against 0/6 on 08-27, when all six ended at /sorry. The remaining 2 (uk#1, us#1) still end at google.com/sorry with the block heuristic fired: the unchanged ACCESS problem, reported as a block. As on google_search_chromium, the wait-strategy fix is confirmed by the absence of any run that stops on the interstitial shell with a clean 200 and 0 rows. NOTE for the literal-match trap: a German shopping SERP for 'laptop' is full of model names and scores badly against the query word -- these pages were read and are healthy. CALLER TIMEOUT, CONFIRMED: one attempt of this preset now costs ~36s -- every google run in the 08-28 record carries "attempt 1/3 shortened to ~36000ms of the requested 45000ms to fit the page-task ceiling" (measured 35.7-36.4s) -- and a job that spends all three attempts reached took_ms 59058 (google_search_chromium/us) and 57193 (google_search_camoufox/us), before any queue wait. `/api/v1/search?engine=google` materializes google_search_chromium with no wait_until/wait_for_selector/timeout_ms override (src/api/search.py:68 and 242-248), so it inherits these numbers verbatim, and yozh-law-checker's backend/app/services/scraper_search_client.py:27 calls /api/v1/search with `timeout=60` and has four `return None` degrade paths. THAT CLIENT IS NOT AFFECTED TODAY: it calls the endpoint only with engine="yandex", which routes to yandex_search_camoufox and is untouched by this change. The consequence is conditional on that client switching to engine="google", at which point a blocked or retrying Google job legitimately outlives its 60s budget and the caller receives None with nothing to log, indistinguishable from an empty SERP. OPERATOR ACTION, IF AND WHEN THAT SWITCH HAPPENS: raise that client's timeout to at least 90s (clear of the 59.1s worst job measured here, still under PAGE_TASK_TIMEOUT_S=120s), or -- if 60s is a hard product constraint -- log the timeout degrade distinctly so "we gave up waiting" is never reported as "Google returned nothing".
